title: Mashed cauliflower
summary: Steamed cauliflower whipped with butter, cream and garlic until smooth enough to stand in for mashed potatoes.

ingredients.note: one large head, cut into florets

steps: Steam the cauliflower and garlic over boiling water for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides through the thickest stem with no resistance.
Tip into a colander and let it steam-dry for 5 minutes; wet cauliflower makes a runny mash. Press gently with a clean towel to remove more water.
Blend or process the hot cauliflower and garlic with the butter, warm cream, salt and pepper until smooth, scraping down once. For a rougher texture use a potato masher instead.
Taste for salt, spoon into a warm dish and scatter the chives over the top.

swaps.note: use the thick part from the top of the can

dairy_free_notes: Coconut milk gives a faintly sweet note that the garlic mostly hides; a little extra salt and pepper balances it.
tips: Make it ahead and reheat in a covered dish at 175 °C (350 °F) for 20 minutes, stirring once.

origin.history: Recipes for mashing boiled potatoes with butter and milk appear in English cookbooks by the mid-1700s, and the dish spread with the potato across Europe and North America. Mashing cauliflower in its place is a modern idea, taken up by low-carb home cooks in the United States from the late 1990s onward.
